sides.name: Egypt (Second and Third Field Armies)
sides.note: Strength: five infantry divisions each reinforced by an armoured brigade; 'over 100,000 combat troops and 1,020 tanks' crossed 6-9 Oct (Gawrych, Leavenworth Paper 21); Wikipedia: 100,000 soldiers, 1,350 tanks and 2,000 guns and heavy mortars deployed for the assault, 32,000 infantry in the first waves; Egypt total 1,700 tanks, 2,400 APCs, 400 combat aircraft, 140 helicopters, 150 SAM batteries (62 in the front line). Armor high includes the 4th and 21st Armoured Divisions held west of the canal until 14 Oct. infantry_line ~90% of the crossing force, educated; ifv_apc = share of the 2,400 APCs with the two field armies, educated. Air split educated (MiG-21 vs Su-7/MiG-17). Objective: the passes were the stated aim of the 14 Oct offensive; the original plan (Badr) sought only a 10-15 km bridgehead under the SAM umbrella. Tech (derived:tech-anchor, 1973 between 8 and 9): weapons 8.7 (Sagger ATGM, RPG-7, SA-6 guided missiles approach the 1985 anchor); fortification 8.3 (SAM belt, ramparts). Ratings: command 0.55 (excellent crossing staff work, rigid after 9 Oct, 14 Oct offensive outside SAM cover failed); morale 0.8; training 0.55 (drilled for the crossing). Surprise complete (Gawrych). riverCrossing true: the Egyptian offensive opened with an assault crossing of the Suez Canal against the Bar-Lev Line (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Badr_(1973)). objective kind capture: Ismail and Sadat overruled Shazly to seize the Mitla and Gidi Passes and Refidim in the 14 October offensive, which failed (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War).

sides.name: Israel (Southern Command)
sides.note: Start (6 Oct): ~450 men of the Jerusalem Brigade in 16 Bar-Lev forts and 290 tanks in three armoured brigades of the Sinai Division (Wikipedia); infantry high adds the division's mechanised infantry. Reinforcements: day 2 (8 Oct) Adan's 162nd Division (three brigades, 183 tanks + a 44-tank mechanised brigade, Wikipedia) and Sharon's 143rd Division (~200 tanks, educated); day 7-8 further reserves (Magen's division, repaired tanks) bringing the front to 700-750 tanks by 14 Oct (Wikipedia). Artillery and reinforcement infantry are educated guesses. Air: IAF 440 combat aircraft for both fronts; ~half assigned to Sinai, educated split (Mirage/Nesher/F-4 fighters, A-4/F-4 strike). Tech: air 8.8 (F-4E) but heavily attrited by SA-6/SA-2 belt; logistics 8.3 (plus US airlift from 14 Oct). Ratings: command 0.6 (Gonen's failed 8 Oct counterattack, later successful Deversoir crossing); morale 0.8 (existential); training 0.75. Fortified flag false: Bar-Lev forts were too thinly held to act as fortified positions. prepared false: the surprise crossing hit only 450 soldiers in 16 Bar-Lev forts and 290 tanks in all of Sinai, so the Dovecote defence was never manned as planned (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War). objective kind capture: Israel's decisive aim was the canal crossing at Deversoir at the northern edge of Great Bitter Lake, through the gap between the Egyptian Second and Third Armies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yom_Kippur_War).

outcome.note: 6 Oct - first ceasefire 22 Oct (16 days), final halt 24-25 Oct. Winner coded Israel on the military outcome at the ceasefire (Third Army encircled with 30,000-45,000 men, IDF 101 km from Cairo, 1,600 km2 west of the canal) but contested: Egypt held ~1,200 km2 on the east bank and achieved its political aim. Egypt: 5,000-15,000 dead, 8,372 captured (whole war, nearly all Sinai), wounded unknown (educated ~12,000-30,000). Israel: war total 2,521-2,800 killed, 7,250-8,800 wounded, 293 captured (Wikipedia; Gawrych: 2,800+ killed, 7,500 wounded); Sinai share ~two thirds is an educated split (Chinese Farm alone ~300 dead, 1,000 wounded). Grade C on losses.
